findings.title: Team admin permission check is inverted: requires being both admin AND owner
findings.body:
The team permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
    (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
    (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This means the user must be BOTH admin AND owner to be granted permission. A team admin (who is not an owner) is incorrectly denied. The variable name and intent clearly indicate either role should be sufficient. Compare with the rest of the codebase where similar checks use `||`. As written, almost no legitimate user passes this branch unless they happen to be both.

findings.title: Any existing attendee can add arbitrary third parties to a booking
Case-sensitive comparison against existing attendee emails allows duplicates
Calendar update uses the requesting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
Guests persisted to DB before calendar/email side-effects, with no rollback
findings.body: The flow is: `prisma.booking.update` (commits new attendees) -> `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` -> `sendAddGuestsEmails` (wrapped only in a `console.log` on error). There is no transaction and no compensation. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., bad credentials, video provider error), the guests remain in the database but never receive an invite; the caller sees a TRPC error and may retry, creating duplicates. If email sending fails it is silently swallowed, so the UI reports success while the new guest never receives notification. Either wrap everything in a transaction with rollback, or reverse the order (validate-then-side-effect-then-persist) and surface failures properly.

findings.title: Email-sending failure is silently logged, but the mutation still returns success
Allows adding guests to cancelled or already-completed bookings
findings.body: After loading the booking there is no check on `booking.status`. A user can add guests to a `CANCELLED`, `REJECTED`, or past `ACCEPTED` booking. `sendAddGuestsEmails` will still send a 'guests added' notification and `updateCalendarAttendees` will still push an updated invite for an event that is no longer happening. Guard against `booking.status === BookingStatus.CANCELLED` (and arguably against bookings in the past).

findings.title: New guests are inserted with empty name and the organizer's timezone/locale
findings.body:
Each new guest row is created with:

```ts
{ name: "", email: guest, timeZone: organizer.timeZone, locale: organizer.locale }
```

An empty `name` will render as a blank attendee in the UI (booking list, emails, calendar) and confuses no-show/dropdown flows. Also forcing the organizer's timezone/locale means the new guest's localized email content and meeting-time display are wrong. Either ask for a name in the dialog (it currently does not), or at minimum leave name nullable/derive a placeholder, and use a sensible default locale (e.g., `en`).

findings.title: Newly added guests receive the original 'meeting scheduled' confirmation instead of an 'added to meeting' notification
`booking?.userPrimaryEmail` is not a known Booking field
findings.body: The calendar event uses `email: booking?.userPrimaryEmail ?? organizer.email`. The Prisma `Booking` model exposes `user` (relation) and `userId`, but I cannot find a `userPrimaryEmail` column on the Booking model in this diff's context. If it doesn't exist on `booking`, this will be `undefined` and the fallback `organizer.email` is used; otherwise the column may silently return `null` and bypass the intended primary-email selection. Verify the field exists; if not, drop the `??` or fetch from the user relation explicitly.

findings.title: addGuests uses authedProcedure instead of bookingsProcedure
findings.body: All sibling booking mutations in this router (`editLocation`) are wrapped with `bookingsProcedure` which presumably enforces booking-level authorization. `addGuests` uses the bare `authedProcedure`, leaving all access control to the handler. The handler has the permission bugs described above, so any logged-in user who can hit this endpoint relies entirely on a handler bug-free. Switch to `bookingsProcedure` for consistency and defense-in-depth.

findings.title: Client-side uniqueness/email validation is misleading and not exhaustive
findings.body: The schema is `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(... unique ...)`, and a failed parse just sets `isInvalidEmail` and shows the generic 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' message. Initial state is `[""]`, so the dialog is invalid out of the box; the message does not indicate which entry is bad, nor does it surface the empty-string case specifically. Empty inputs should be filtered before validation, and per-field errors should be shown (or the Add button should be disabled while the list is invalid). The server's handler also does case-sensitive dedupe, so two entries differing only in case slip through here as 'unique' but cause a duplicate downstream.

findings.title: Uses array index as React key for email fields
findings.body: `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}>...)`. When a user removes an item in the middle of the list, every input after it is re-bound to the wrong value (because React reuses the DOM and state by index). Use a stable key (e.g., the email value itself or a generated id) so removing index N doesn't corrupt the remaining inputs.

findings.title: No automated tests for a new permission-sensitive mutation with email and calendar side-effects
findings.body: The PR adds a new tRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` that mutates the DB, calls calendar/video integrations, and dispatches emails. There are no unit tests, integration tests, or e2e tests included. Given the multiple authorization bugs (admin+owner check, attendee-as-actor, case-sensitive dedupe, wrong credentials) and side-effect ordering issues already found in this review, at minimum a test suite covering: (1) team admin can add, team member cannot; (2) attendee cannot add; (3) case-insensitive duplicate is rejected; (4) cancelled booking is rejected; (5) calendar/email failures are surfaced, must be added before merge.
